notice.label: Biographical note
notice.title: Biographical <t>note</t>
notice.text: Nagy Habib (born Cairo, 1952) is a British-Egyptian hepatobiliary surgeon and Professor of Hepatobiliary Surgery at Imperial College London, where he has held a chair in the Department of Surgery and Cancer since 2003 and is Academic Head of HPB Surgery. He studied medicine at Ain Shams University, Cairo, trained in surgery with Henri Bismuth and Thomas Starzl, and is a Fellow of the Royal College of Surgeons of Edinburgh. His work spans liver, pancreatic and biliary surgery at Hammersmith Hospital; radiofrequency techniques for liver resection, from which the Habib 4X and Habib EndoHPB instruments were developed; and translational research in liver disease, including early clinical trials of adenovirus gene therapy, autologous stem cells and small activating RNA. From 2007 he served as Imperial’s Pro-Rector for Commercial Affairs. He was elected to the Académie Nationale de Chirurgie in 2015.

chronology.label: Chronology
chronology.title: Chronology, <t>1952–2026</t>
items: Fellow of the Royal College of Surgeons of Edinburgh.
First living-related liver transplant in Africa and the Middle East.
Editor, <t>Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Methods and Protocols</t>, Humana Press.
Clinical trial of an E1B-deleted adenovirus for primary and secondary liver tumours. EMcision formed as a spin-out from Imperial College London.
Radiofrequency liver resection by heat coagulative necrosis, <t>Annals of Surgery</t>.
Professor of Hepatobiliary Surgery, Imperial College London.
Habib 4X introduced, with FDA clearance and CE mark.
Pro-Rector for Commercial Affairs, Imperial College London.
Invited speaker, Henri Bismuth Symposium, Jerusalem.
MiNA Therapeutics, with Robert Habib as founding chief executive.
Elected to the Académie Nationale de Chirurgie.
Invited by the Vatican to advise on regenerative medicine.
EMcision and the Habib EndoHPB acquired by Boston Scientific.
First-in-human trial of MTL-CEBPA, <t>Clinical Cancer Research</t>.
Invited speaker, American Association of Cell & Gene Therapy.
Research and Funding Sub-Committee, Royal College of Surgeons of Edinburgh. Trustee, MPS Society.

clinical.label: Clinical work
clinical.title: Clinical <t>work</t>
items: Liver, pancreatic and biliary surgery at Hammersmith Hospital, London.
Division of the liver after coagulation of the transection plane by radiofrequency energy, known as Habib’s resection. Published in <t>Annals of Surgery</t>, 2002.
The first in Africa and the Middle East, 1993; reported in <t>International Surgery</t> the same year.
Applied to the liver, pancreas and kidney. <t>Digestive Surgery</t>, 2012.
